science.qualification: Photosphere color from the star's measured spectrum (Kharitonov, Tereshchenko & Knyazeva (1988), Spectrophotometric Catalogue of Stars (Alma-Ata), record 1125). The disc is unresolved: no map or absolute brightness is implied. Self-luminous, so no lighting. The disc is dimmed toward the limb by the power law I(mu) = mu^0.231 that Martinez et al. (2021), ApJ 916, 60 fit to the star's resolved disc (CHARA/MIRC H band, 1.5-1.7 um; not a visible band).

science.label: September 2011
science.description: Brightness of λ Andromedae's surface in the CHARA/MIRC H band (1.49-1.73 um), eight channels, fitted with ROTIR to the 2,984 squared visibilities and 3,704 closure phases mirc measured on 6 nights, 2 to 24 September 2011: one surface on a sphere 2.742 mas across that turns once in 54.2 d, tilted 85.63° from the line of sight with its pole 26.09° east of north (Martinez et al. (2021), ApJ 916, 60, Table 4 (https). The fit leaves a reduced chi-squared of 1.72 on the squared visibilities and 2.30 on the closure phases, where a spotless star leaves 3.13 and 28.29 (limit 3); its spots are 2.14 times those the same fit draws on a spotless star of 2.77 mas (limit 2); and two independent halves of the data give the same spots (correlation 0.83, limit 0.5). Percent of the mean of the surface seen. Longitude 0 is the meridian that faced the Earth on 14 September 2011. Nothing smaller than about 21° of the surface is resolved. The 34° of longitude that faced the Earth on none of the nights hold the mean, inside the black line. The same nights were imaged by their authors (Martinez et al. (2021), ApJ 916, 60; Parks et al. (2021), ApJ 913, 54); this is a reduction made in this project with their code, not their published map.
science.title: mirc · surface map made here · September 2011

science.label: Color + brightness
science.description: The star's color (#ffddbb, its Color dataset) over the surface map this project made from mirc interferometry of 2 to 24 September 2011: the map's scale, 70% to 130% of the mean surface, runs from a darker, richer tone of the same hue to the color itself. The map is of infrared light (CHARA/MIRC H band (1.49-1.73 um), eight channels), where the darkest region gives 35% less light than the brightest; how much darker the spots are in visible light is not measured, and no color change is drawn. Longitude 0 is the meridian that faced the Earth on 14 September 2011. The 34° of longitude that never faced the Earth on these nights hold the mean. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: mirc · the star in its color over its surface map · 2 to 24 September 2011
